SRC-041:R001.text: SILO text-history ownership is identity-based: a structural reorder, insert, delete, swap or transfer with unchanged logical SILO text creates zero text-history transitions; previous committed text derives from committed slot rows plus committed identity mapping diffed against the current identity-to-text map; committed baselines advance only after successful publication.

SRC-041:R002.text: Persistent undo and redo acknowledge durable publication: the apply step returns explicit success or failure, the recovery cursor advances only after a successful forced authoritative save, and on save failure or exception the pre-step value is restored, the cursor stays unchanged, no reverse history is manufactured, and unrelated dirty domains are preserved.

SRC-041:R003.text: Archive lineage dirty ownership derives from the canonical active SILO owner used by active silo identity resolution, never a nonexistent showing_archive attribute; legitimate unsaved archive edits produce no false lineage refusal while genuine identity or text mismatch still fails closed.

SRC-041:R004.text: Restore establishes a monotonic external-writer boundary: snapshot issuance is separated from physical execution so an issued snapshot is never re-registered, every issued snapshot carries a publication epoch required to equal the current epoch at the final replace gate, revocation is monotonic and idempotent, and the Sync-Project writer barrier is established under the canonical mutation gate before destructive restore publication without lock inversion.
